sources.why: Anker blog: general sizing advice, own brand only, no runtimes given
sources.evidence: Start with runtime, not output size. Once your modem and router are within the power station's wattage limit, the battery capacity decides how long your WiFi can stay on.

sources.why: Generic how-to on a vercel site, no models or runtimes
sources.evidence: A small router UPS may work for short outages, while a portable power station is better if you also need a laptop, phone charger or light.

sources.why: Outage plan article; the text given names no product or runtime
sources.evidence: For most short outages, the difference between misery and comfort is smaller: keep the Wi-Fi on, keep the phones charged, keep the lights on, and top up the laptop.

sources.why: Anker UK blog, vague 'hours' claim, own brand only
sources.evidence: A router draws very little power, so a portable power station keeps your Wi-Fi online for hours.

missing: A named shortlist of small power stations, each with measured router-plus-modem runtime in hours at a real load of about 15–30W, UPS switchover time, current prices and a direct pick.
why: No major reviewer or authority shows up. The two readable pages from a known name are Anker's own blogs, which only cover Anker and give vague runtimes. The other readable pages are a generic how-to and an outage plan with no products named. Seven of the twelve results came back with no text at all. A focused page that names models and gives measured runtimes for a router and modem, with prices, would stand out.
